# mdstudio

> mdstudio is an open-source, local-first Markdown editor and portability checker. The preview follows the rules of the target you pick, flags syntax that will not travel, and exports clean .md files. With an account you can edit a draft together with invited people, share a read-only copy for review, and publish to GitHub. Formerly called Markdown Studio.

Write Markdown in a full-featured editor with a formatting toolbar and a live preview. The raw Markdown is the single source of truth: the preview shows what the target renders, with no preview-only syntax. Drafts are saved in the browser (IndexedDB) with no account and are not uploaded unless the writer chooses to. An optional account keeps up to 5 chosen drafts in a cloud by default.

## What it does

- Target profiles: Strict CommonMark, GFM extended, GFM without HTML, Wiki notes. The preview, the checks and the toolbar warnings follow the chosen profile.
- Portability checker: flags raw HTML, local image paths, base64 images, wiki-links, math, Mermaid and trailing-space line breaks, with clickable issues that jump to the line. Rules can be turned on or off, with publication standards and the writer's own text or regex rules.
- Editing together: up to 3 invited people edit one draft at the same time, online or offline, with live cursors and per-person undo. Edits made offline merge when the network returns.
- Review: share a read-only copy that expires after 1 to 7 days, public or limited to named people, with comments from signed-in readers.
- Publishing: commit or pull request to a GitHub repository with images beside the file, or publish a gist. Needs an account with a confirmed email.
- Rich Markdown: tables, task lists, footnotes, GitHub alerts, KaTeX math, Mermaid diagrams, syntax-highlighted code blocks.
- Import and export: open .md files, ZIP archives or whole folders, paste from Google Docs, Notion and the web; export clean UTF-8 Markdown (LF endings), standalone HTML, or every draft as a ZIP.
- Library: search drafts and the words inside them, filter by tag, organise folders, and go back to any earlier version with a side-by-side compare.
- Optional AI writing helpers with the writer's own API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Keys stay in session memory and requests go directly from the browser to the provider; every change is shown as a diff first.
- Works offline after the first visit and can be installed as an app.
- MIT licensed and open source. Self-host with Docker (`ghcr.io/deityhub/mdstudio` or `deityhub/mdstudio` on Docker Hub).

## Who it is for

- People who write for the web and publish in more than one place.
- Developers who write READMEs and docs, and want a second pair of eyes before the pull request.
- Notes writers who share outside their notes app.
- Small teams who review and edit docs together without leaving Markdown.

## Common questions

- Is it open source? Yes, it is MIT licensed, and you can use it in the browser or self-host it.
- Do I need an account? No. An account is optional and adds cloud drafts (up to 5 by default), editing together, share links with comments, and publishing to GitHub.
- Are documents private? Yes by default. They stay in the browser; a draft goes to the cloud only if the writer chooses, and is public only if published as a link that expires.
- How is it different from other Markdown editors? Most render Markdown their own way. mdstudio renders strictly and tells you where the target will differ. It is where you write, check, review and publish from, not a notes app or a blog host.

## Guides

- [Portable Markdown: why it renders differently everywhere](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/markdown-portability): the six things that break most often and a checklist
- [CommonMark vs GitHub Flavored Markdown](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/commonmark-vs-github-flavored-markdown): tables, task lists, strikethrough, footnotes, alerts
- [Obsidian to GitHub Markdown](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/obsidian-to-github-markdown): converting wiki-links, highlights, callouts and embeds
- [Writing Markdown for dev.to and Hashnode](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/markdown-for-devto-and-hashnode): front matter, images, raw HTML
- [Markdown line breaks and paragraphs](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/markdown-line-breaks): soft breaks, hard breaks and the portable choice
- [Markdown images](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/markdown-images): paths, hosted URLs, base64 and alt text
- [Math and Mermaid diagrams in Markdown](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/markdown-math-and-diagrams): where they render and what to do elsewhere
